To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

spectral counting is a good method of protein quantitation for correlative analysis with gene expression and that the correlation of protein and gene expression data is dependent on the biological context.

spectral count based methods are comparable to intensity-based methods for the purpose of correlating gene and protein expression levels, and that the use of RNA-Seq data as a benchmark for proteomics studies should be done with caution.
spectral count based measures of protein abundance are comparable to intensity-based measures with respect to the correlation with gene expression.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of protein abundance estimation method has a relatively minor impact on the correlation between protein and gene expression data.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of protein abundance estimation method does not have a substantial impact on the correlation between gene expression and protein abundance data.

the spectral count based protein quantification method is comparable to the widely used intensity based approach in terms of the correlation with gene expression, and that the correlation between gene- and protein-level measurements can be improved by using a combination of multiple normalization strategies.
, for the purpose of correlation analysis of gene and proteomic expression data, spectral count based measures of protein expression are as good as intensity based measures.
